instance_recommendations.rationale: AMD EPYC-based alternative with identical vCPU/memory specs at ~10% lower cost. Best price-performance ratio among all alternatives. Ideal for compute-heavy Celery workers where marginal single-thread performance differences between Intel and AMD are negligible for task processing throughput.

Newer-generation AMD (3rd gen EPYC) with slightly better per-core performance than c5a at nearly the same price point. Offers a good balance of cost savings and improved IPC, making it a strong second choice.
Current baseline instance type. No migration risk or compatibility concerns. Retain as fallback if AMD-based instances exhibit any application-specific incompatibilities.

Same price as c5.2xlarge but with 3rd gen Intel Xeon (Ice Lake) offering ~15% better compute per core. No cost savings but better throughput per instance, which can reduce the number of instances needed at peak, indirectly lowering fleet cost.

rationale.scaling_policy: The step thresholds are aligned with observed queue depth percentiles. The p50 is ~310 messages, so the boundary at 300 separates the median steady-state from scale-up territory. Below 50 messages (well under the ~28% zero-depth periods), aggressive scale-down (-20) reclaims capacity quickly. The 50-300 band applies moderate scale-down (-5) to avoid oscillation around the median. Scale-up steps at 1000, 5000, 12000, and 35000 correspond roughly to increasing severity: 1000 is above p50 indicating building backlog, 5000 approaches p95 (~11.5k), 12000 exceeds p95 requiring aggressive response, and 35000 exceeds p99 (~32.4k) triggering maximum scale-out of +80 to handle extreme bursts up to the observed max of ~115k. The current policy's -100 scale-down at 0-100 is dangerously aggressive and risks scaling to near-zero too fast; the revised two-tier scale-down (0-50 and 50-300) is more graduated.
rationale.strategy_impact: The balanced strategy favors moderate cooldowns and percentile-aligned thresholds. The 300-second cooldown equals the instance drain time (the binding constraint), ensuring instances fully drain before further terminations, while also exceeding the 120s warmup. The graduated scale-down avoids the current policy's all-or-nothing -100 adjustment which can cause capacity whiplash. Scale-up steps are sized to reach the observed max_desired of 181 within 2-3 scaling actions for extreme bursts, keeping queue latency manageable without over-provisioning. Instance recommendations prioritize the c5a.2xlarge for ~10% savings with equivalent specs, consistent with a balanced cost-performance approach.
rationale.risk_notes: 1) The observed max_desired of 181 is within the max_size of 250, providing adequate headroom; do not reduce max_size below 181. 2) The 27.58% zero-depth period is well below the 80% threshold, so scaling to zero is not recommended; min_size should remain at 1. 3) Switching to AMD-based instances (c5a/c6a) should be validated with a canary deployment to confirm no application-level incompatibilities. 4) The current policies have null/0 cooldown which risks runaway scaling; the 300s cooldown is critical to prevent launch storms during rapid queue depth fluctuations. 5) Peak traffic at 22:00 UTC with trough at 06:00 UTC suggests a predictable daily pattern; if workload becomes more predictable, consider adding a scheduled scaling action to pre-warm capacity before peak hours to complement this reactive policy.
